names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 26 iunie, «Sfântul Cuvios David din Tesalonic».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 26 Ιουνίου, «Όσιος Δαβίδ από τη Θεσσαλονίκη», with the rank word and the city left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 26. јун ст. ст., „Преподобни Давид“ — Преподобни is the rank, which `types` already carries, and the bare forename is the whole of the rest: **the heading is two words long and one of them is the rank**, for the second day running. The «of Thessalonica» of the display name is the corpus’s own, off the city both other books name, and §10 reserves it. **THE FOLD IS THE WIDEST THIS READER HAS WRITTEN AND IS MEASURED BOTH WAYS.** `foldchk.py` returns **seven** other holders of the exact string «Давид» and `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` returns the same seven for the gate’s own folded key, so this folder is the eighth: `david-of-gareji`, `david-of-georgia`, `david-of-hermopolis`, `david-son-of-prince-theodore`, `david-son-of-vukan`, `david-the-builder` and `gleb-prince-and-passion-bearer`. **The last of those is not a David at all**: the form is on his folder in `ru` because David was his baptismal name, which is the same shape as the Germanus of Kazan entry the gate already carries for «Григорий». The heading offers nothing to break the fold with. A `READ_FOLDS` key is added in the same commit, writing the row and registering the fold being two acts.

birth.note: saint.gr, as the folder's own life has it: a native of northern Mesopotamia, «born about 450». The Romanian calendar parts from it about his birth, which the life records.

death.note: saint.gr, as the folder's own life has it: «He died at sea as the ship rounded the headland, between 535 and 541».

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 26 iunie — «Sfântul Cuvios David din Tesalonic»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 26ης Ιουνίου — «Όσιος Δαβίδ από τη Θεσσαλονίκη»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 26 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the almond tree settles the identity — the dendrite of Thessalonica, with the archbishop Aristides, the embassy to Justinian and the monastery of the Aproïtai. The two sources disagree about his birth: the folder's Romanian life has him born and brought up in Thessalonica, while saint.gr says «καταγόταν από τη βόρεια Μεσοποταμία … και γεννήθηκε περί το 450 μ.Χ.» and has him come to the city with a monk called Adolas. Both readings are set down in the life and neither is preferred here. No `dates` object is proposed, because the years — about 450, and a death between 535 and 541 — come from this second source alone. He is the first of two Davids saint.gr prints on this day; the other, the new venerable-martyr of Kydonies, is a new folder in this batch. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 09.07.2026 (26. јун ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Давид“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry and its only person. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 26 June is the same menologion number this folder’s Romanian and Greek rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed; the Russian row stays `undocumented`. **IDENTIFIED ON THE SCENE, WHICH THE HEADING MADE NECESSARY: IT IS TWO WORDS AND ONE OF THEM IS THE RANK.** „Преподобни Давид“ gives a bare forename and nothing else, and the corpus keeps **two** Davids on the menologion 26/6 — this one and `david-of-kydonies` — so the name settles nothing. The body settles it in three sentences: „Родом Солуњанин.“, a Thessalonian by birth; „Најпре се подвизавао близу Солуна у једној колиби, направљеној под бадемовим дрветом.“, he first struggled near Thessalonica in a hut built under an almond tree; and „Доцније продужио подвиг свој у Тесалији.“, he later continued his struggle in Thessaly. The almond tree and Thessalonica are this folder’s own story and `david-of-kydonies` is a new martyr of another age. **Identified on the scene and not on the name.** **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THIS IS THE CLEAREST REFUSAL OF A NARROWING THE WAVE HAS MET.** „Упокојио се мирно, и преселио у блажену вечност 540. године.“ — he reposed peacefully and passed over into blessed eternity in the year **540**. The folder holds `death` earliest 535, latest 541, display «535–541», off saint.gr as its own life has it: «He died at sea as the ship rounded the headland, between 535 and 541». **540 falls inside that range**, so writing it would narrow a source’s stated interval by six years on the authority of a second book that states no interval at all. A narrowing is refused, and there is nothing to widen either: the two books do not disagree, 540 being one of the seven years the Greek page allows. `death` is untouched, and so is `birth` c. 450, which is also saint.gr’s and which this book gives no year for. **Nothing is averaged, nothing is preferred, and the agreement is recorded in the prose instead of in the field.** **BUT THE TWO BOOKS CONTRADICT EACH OTHER FLATLY ABOUT WHERE HE CAME FROM, AND ABOUT HOW HE DIED.** The origin: „Родом Солуњанин.“ makes him a Thessalonian by birth, where saint.gr makes him «a native of northern Mesopotamia» — and this folder’s own note already records that the Romanian calendar parts from saint.gr about his birth, so there were two readings of it before this book arrived and there are three now. The death: this book has him repose **peacefully**, where saint.gr has him **die at sea as the ship rounded the headland**. Both are written in the life and neither is chosen, and neither bears on a field. **No `locations`**: Thessalonica, Thessaly and Mesopotamia are named in clauses, and a located saint who reads as alive over a century is the thing `map-span.test.mjs` exists for. **`types` UNTOUCHED.** Преподобни is `venerable`, which the folder carries beside `ascetic` and `wonderworker`. „Толико се очистио постом, молитвом и бдењем, да се удостојио примити велику благодат од Бога.“ and „Многобројним чудесима својим задивио је људе.“ — he so purified himself by fasting, prayer and vigil that he was counted worthy to receive great grace from God, and he amazed people by his numerous wonders — corroborate the `ascetic` and the `wonderworker` that are already there, and a type already held is not written twice. A rank read out of a verb in a body is not written at all. No `office`. **NO ROWS. THE EMPEROR HE CENSED IS NOT EVEN NAMED.** „Једном је узео жара на руку, метнуо тамјан, и окадио цара, без икакве повреде руке своје.“ and „Видећи то, цар му се поклони до земље.“ — once he took live coals in his hand, laid incense on them and censed the emperor without any hurt to his hand, and seeing it the emperor bowed to the ground before him. The book calls him цар and gives him no name, so there is nothing to identify and nothing to refuse: an emperor in a life is not automatically a relation and an unnamed one is not a candidate. `macarius-makres` and `symeon-of-the-wonderful-mountain` are `related` here already, this book names neither of them, and both rows are left exactly as they were. **THE OTHER THREE ENTRIES ARE ICONS AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS A FOLDER OR A ROW.** „Празник иконе Тихфинске“, „Празник иконе Одигитрије“ and „Празник Богородичине иконе Лидске, или Римљанке“ — the feasts of the Tikhvin icon, of the Hodegetria and of the Lydda icon, also called the Roman. Празник is a feast by §5’s own ruling and an icon is not a person, so **three of the day’s four entries produce nothing**, which is the thinnest day of this reader’s range. They are recorded because of what they name. „Ова икона Пресвете Богородице била је најпре у Цариграду, но на седамдесет година пред пад Цариграда, 1383. године, она се изненадно појави на ваздуху близу града Тихфина у северној Русији.“ — the icon was first at Constantinople, and seventy years before the fall of Constantinople, in the year 1383, it appeared suddenly in the air near the town of Tikhvin in northern Russia: **the arithmetic of that sentence is the book’s own and it is sound**, 1453 less seventy being 1383, which is worth recording after two days on which its arithmetic was not. A year of an icon’s appearance is nobody’s date. „Ову је икону радио на дрвету сам јеванђелист Лука. Њу је видела Пресвета Богородица и благословила је.“ has the Hodegetria painted on wood by the evangelist Luke himself and blessed by the Mother of God who saw it, „Ту икону свети Лука подарио је державном Теофилу, за кога је писао Дела светих апостола.“ has Luke give it to the Theophilus for whom he wrote the Acts of the Apostles, and „Из Антиохије икона се доцније пренесе у Јерусалим, а из Јерусалима узме је царица Евдокија и пошаље у Цариград царевој сестри, побожној Пулхерији, на дар.“ and „Пулхерија је положи у Влахерну цркву, своју сопствену задужбину.“ carry it from Antioch to Jerusalem, thence by the empress Eudocia to Constantinople as a gift to the emperor’s pious sister Pulcheria, who laid it in her own foundation at Blachernae. **Not one of those four takes a row**: the subject of each of those entries is an icon, a dedication is not a relation, and the object of a wonder is not its subject. „Када војске персијског цара Хозроја и скитског Кагана ударише на Цариград, патријарх Сергије изнесе ову икону на бедеме градске, и ношаше је по бедему.“ and „Од тада је установљен спомен овога чуда Пресвете Богородице у суботу пете недеље Часног Поста са читањем Акатиста.“ have the patriarch Sergius carry the icon along the walls against the armies of the Persian Chosroes and the Scythian Khagan, and the commemoration of the wonder set thereafter on the Saturday of the fifth week of the Fast with the reading of the Akathist — **which is the same patriarch Sergius the previous day’s entry named as the Akathist’s composer**, two consecutive days of one book cross-referring, and still no folder: there are nine multi-word Sergius folders in this corpus and not one is a patriarch of Constantinople. **A feast that is a Pascha offset is not this corpus’ to hold off a line like this**, and nothing was written for it. „У време иконоборства ова икона би пренета у обитељ Пантократора и тамо зазидана у зид, и би остављено кандило пред њом да гори. Како је зазидана, онако је после и нађена.“ — in the time of the iconoclasm it was taken to the house of the Pantokrator and walled up there with a lamp left burning before it, and as it was walled up so it was afterwards found. „Патријарх Генадије пошаље ову икону у Рим за време иконоборства.“ — the patriarch Gennadius sent the Lydda icon to Rome in the time of the iconoclasm, and „Она доплови ту сама брже од било код брода, и кад се иконоборци уморише од свог прогона она доплови назад у Цариград истим путем.“ has it sail there by itself faster than any ship and sail back the same way when the iconoclasts had tired of their persecution. **That sentence does not sit with itself**: a patriarch Gennadius of Constantinople belongs to the fifth century and the iconoclasm to the eighth and ninth. It is the book’s own and a reader does not repair a source; it is recorded here and nothing is derived from it. **AND FOUR FOLDERS THE CORPUS KEEPS ON THIS MENOLOGION NUMBER THIS BOOK DOES NOT NAME**: `anthion`, `david-of-kydonies`, `dionysius-of-suzdal` and `john-of-gothia`. That is not a refusal and nobody is left out for want of a folder — the Prologue simply keeps one of the five, and says so by printing one person. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. THE VERSE IS NOT USED, AND READING IT CORRECTED A CLAIM THIS GENERATOR HAD ALREADY MADE. The ПЕСМА for 26 June is twenty lines on the **Lydda icon**, the fourth entry, and not a word on the day’s one person; the first draft of this note said it was on the Hodegetria, which was a guess and was wrong, and the uncommitted batch was restored and rebuilt rather than patched. §3 puts the verse in no field and in no life, but it had to be quoted here, because **the verse and the prose of this one book name two different patriarchs for the same act.** The prose, „Патријарх Генадије пошаље ову икону у Рим за време иконоборства.“, makes it Патријарх Генадије. The verse, „Икону Лидску Богоматере Патријарх Герман, заточеник вере, Испосла папи из Цариграда Кад за иконе исток пострада.“, makes it Germanus, a prisoner of the faith, who sent it to the pope out of Constantinople when the East suffered for the icons. **And the verse is the one that fits the chronology the prose broke**: a patriarch Germanus of Constantinople belongs to the iconoclasm and a patriarch Gennadius to the fifth century. The reader does not choose between them and does not mend either: both are written here, neither is in a field, no folder is made and no row is taken, and the only reason the verse is quoted at all is that the contradiction is inside one day of one book. „A кад мир златни Исток позлати Икона Лидска дома се врати,“ is where it has the icon come home. It is the fourth day running that the verse treats one entry of several, and the first on which the entry it treats is not a person.

hymns.text: Întru tine părinte cu osârdie s-a mântuit cel după chip; că luând crucea ai urmat lui Hristos; şi lucrând ai învăţat să nu se uite la trup, că este trecător; ci să poarte grijă de suflet, de lucrul cel nemuritor. Pentru aceasta şi cu îngerii împreună se bucură, Preacuvioase Părinte David, duhul tău.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios David din Tesalonic, glasul 8; the text is the common of a venerable father, printed with his name in it.

english.text: In thee, O father, was the image restored with care; for taking up the cross thou didst follow Christ, and by thy works thou didst teach us to overlook the flesh, which passes away, and to care for the soul, a thing immortal. Wherefore thy spirit, O most venerable father David, rejoices together with the angels.

hymns.text: Ὡς φοῖνιξ ἐξήνθησας, τῶν ἀρετῶν τοὺς καρπούς, ἀσκήσας ὡς ἄσαρκος, ἀμυγδαλῆς ἐν φυτῷ, Δαβὶδ Πάτερ Ὅσιε. Ὅθεν Θεσσαλονίκη, τοὶς ὀσίοις σου πόνοις, χάριν παρὰ Κυρίου, δαψιλῆ καρπουμένη, γεραίρει ὡς μεσίτην σέ, θερμὸν πρὸς τὸν Κύριον.

source.text: saint.gr, the first of three apolytikia on his own page, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — it names him, «Δαβὶδ Πάτερ Ὅσιε», and names the almond tree and Thessalonica; the second is the common of a venerable one and the third another proper, and only the first is taken

english.text: Like a palm you flowered with the fruits of the virtues, living as an ascetic in an almond tree as though without flesh, venerable father David. Therefore Thessalonica, reaping abundant grace from the Lord through your holy labours, honours you as a fervent mediator with him.

hymns.text: Ὡς μιμητήν, τῶν οὐρανίων τάξεων, καὶ ἀγαθῶν, τῶν ἐπιγείων πάροικον, ἀπαξίως μακαρίζομεν, σὲ ὦ Δαβὶδ θεομακάριστε· τὸν βίον γὰρ ὡς ἄγγελος ἐτέλεσας, καὶ θείων δωρημάτων κατετρύφησας, ἐξ ὧν καὶ ἡμῖν μετάδος Ὅσιε.

source.text: saint.gr, the kontakion on his own page, Ἦχος β’, Τοὺς ἀσφαλεῖς — it names him, «σὲ ὦ Δαβὶδ θεομακάριστε»

english.text: As an imitator of the heavenly orders, and a sojourner among the good things of earth, we call you blessed all unworthily, David blessed of God; for you finished your life as an angel and took your delight in divine gifts, and of these give us a share also, venerable one.
